item.text:
**4B.1 Research Note**

Overall read: **yes, on balance**. In 2024 Lula repeatedly affirmed democratic contestability, free elections, and peaceful alternation in office. The main counterevidence is indirect: his government backed tougher platform-regulation ideas in a polarized information environment, which can be read as a constraint on contestability, but I found no strong 2024 evidence that Lula himself rejected free and fair elections or denied the legitimacy of opposition victory.

- [Discurso do presidente Lula no evento à margem da Assembleia Geral das Nações Unidas “Em defesa da democracia: lutando contra o extremismo”](https://www.gov.br/g20/pt-br/documentos/discursos/discurso-do-presidente-lula-no-evento-a-margem-da-assembleia-geral-das-nacoes-unidas-em-defesa-da-democracia-lutando-contra-o-extremismo) — Governo do Brasil / G20 — 2024-09-24 — Lula said democracy requires free and fair elections, transparent political process, separation of powers, organizing rights, and protection of human rights; he also said democracy is built by each people and cannot be imposed. This is the strongest direct evidence that he accepted power should be contestable through elections. Question IDs: `4B.1` `3B.8`

- [Lula reafirma que não aceita vitória de Maduro sem provas](https://economia.uol.com.br/noticias/reuters/2024/08/30/lula-reafirma-que-nao-aceita-vitoria-de-maduro-sem-provas.htm) — Reuters via UOL — 2024-08-30 — Lula said he would not accept either side’s claimed victory in Venezuela without proof, urged publication of vote records, floated new elections, and called for a suprapartisan electoral committee with international observers. That is direct pro-contestation evidence: he endorsed evidence-based electoral legitimacy, not permanent rule. Question IDs: `4B.1`

- [Lula diz que Bolsonaro não retornará à Presidência e defende candidato jovem para 2026](https://noticias.uol.com.br/ultimas-noticias/reuters/2024/07/02/lula-diz-que-bolsonaro-nao-retornara-a-presidencia-e-defende-candidato-jovem-para-2026.htm) — Reuters via UOL — 2024-07-02 — Lula said Bolsonaro lost the election and would not return, while arguing Brazil should look for a younger candidate for 2026. The line is blunt, but it treats leadership change as electoral and normal, not as a right to rule indefinitely. Question IDs: `4B.1`

- [Brazil to mark anniversary of January 8 attack on democracy](https://www.investing.com/news/world-news/brazil-to-mark-anniversary-of-january-8-attack-on-democracy-3269163) — Reuters via Investing.com — 2024-01-08 — Lula said those who financed, planned, and executed the January 8 coup attempt should be punished. This supports acceptance of elections by rejecting anti-electoral violence, though it is more about post-coup accountability than election procedure itself. Question IDs: `4B.1` `3B.1` `3B.9`

- [Brazil | Freedom House Freedom in the World 2024](https://freedomhouse.org/country/brazil/freedom-world/2024) — Freedom House — 2024 — Freedom House rated Brazil “Free” and described it as a democracy with competitive elections and vibrant public debate. The caveat is that political violence and harassment remained high, so the environment was democratic but stressed. Question IDs: `4B.1` `3B.8` `3B.10`

- [Brazil | Reuters Institute for the Study of Journalism, Digital News Report 2024](https://reutersinstitute.politics.ox.ac.uk/digital-news-report/2024/brazil) — Reuters Institute — 2024-06-17 — The report says Brazil struggled with misinformation and that the government’s fake-news bill would have made platforms responsible for preventing falsehoods and hate speech; the justice minister threatened an hourly fine when Google opposed it. This is the main caveat: it suggests pressure on the information environment, but it is still framed as anti-disinformation rather than anti-election. Question IDs: `4B.1` `3B.8`

Search gap: I did **not** find strong 2024 evidence that Lula personally denied the legitimacy of competitive elections in Brazil, tried to keep power outside elections, or rejected peaceful turnover. The negative evidence is mostly indirect and institutional: platform-regulation pressure, polarization, and the broader post-2022 democratic stress.
